heroHeadline: Araghchi at BRICS Accuses UAE of Active Role in War; Nuclear Talks Deadlocked; Indian Cargo Ship Sinks off Oman; 30+ Vessels Transit Hormuz Under Iranian Terms — Day 77
heroSubtitle: Day 77 (May 15): Iranian FM Abbas Araghchi traveled to New Delhi for the BRICS foreign ministers' meeting, urging member states to condemn the US-Israel war as a violation of international law. In a significant escalation of rhetoric, Araghchi directly accused the UAE of playing an 'active role' in the war against Iran — the first time Tehran has publicly named Abu Dhabi as a belligerent. On the nuclear track, Araghchi confirmed negotiations are deadlocked: both sides have agreed to postpone the enriched uranium issue to later stages due to its complexity. Iran 'never wanted nuclear weapons,' he said, but expressed doubt about US 'seriousness.' Off the Oman coast, an Indian-flagged cargo vessel sank after an attack sparked a fire while en route from Somalia to Sharjah — a major escalation from vessel seizures to outright sinking. In a separate overnight development, more than 30 ships including Chinese-linked vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz under Iran's unilateral 'cooperative passage' framework — the largest single-night movement since the May 4 IRGC control zone. Iran's Senior VP Mohammadreza Aref declared the Strait 'belongs to Iran' and will not be surrendered 'at any price'; Iran's judiciary simultaneously claimed the legal right to seize US-connected oil tankers. Day 76 recap (May 14): Trump-Xi summit joint agreement — Hormuz 'must remain open,' Iran 'can never have nuclear weapon'; Vance says 'progress' on talks; 52 senators demand zero enrichment in any deal; UKMTO reported vessel seized near Fujairah.
